findings.finding: Peers that reported after Liftoff's 12 Aug call printed a strong Jul-Sep for mobile app user-acquisition demand: AppLovin Q3 revenue $2.18bn +55% y/y, about $100m above the top of its own guide 'primarily driven by the core mobile gaming business', Q4 guided $2.365-2.395bn (+8-10% q/q); Unity Vector +126% y/y and +40% q/q, Q4 Strategic Grow guided +105-107% y/y. Against Liftoff's own Q3 guide of flat q/q ($217-222m vs $219.5m in Q2), this argues the category grew sequentially in the quarter Liftoff is reporting. Net of the share-take reading of the same prints (Piper Sandler initiated Neutral $19 on 22 Sep citing AppLovin/Unity pricing and retention pressure), sized as a modest positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LFTO rose 9.4% to $17.15 on 2026-11-05 on the AppLovin/Unity prints alone (StockStory). Only one prior own print: Q2 revenue beat consensus by ~5.6% and the stock fell 20.59% close to close on the flat Q3 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +9.4% day on 5 Nov is the market pricing the read-through. What is not yet in the price is whether Liftoff captured it; if the market believed Liftoff grew in line with the category, the stock would not sit 34% below its June high and below the $23 IPO price with consensus still at or below the guide midpoint ($214.8m on two aggregators).
findings.independence: Unity, a separate company and document: https://mobilegamer.biz/unity-posts-first-profit-since-its-ipo-as-vector-grows-126/ (2026-11-05). Counter-reading from the same entities: Piper Sandler initiation https://longbridge.com/en/news/299791416 (2026-09-22). Price reaction: https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/lfto/news/why-up-down/why-are-liftoff-mobile-lfto-shares-soaring-today (2026-11-05).

findings.finding: Digital Turbine, which runs a mobile app-growth ad platform, reported on 9 Nov, after LFTO's 5 Nov peer rally: fiscal Q2 (Jul-Sep) revenue $178.7m +27% y/y and raised its FY27 revenue outlook to $670-690m from $650-670m, a third independent counterparty confirming Jul-Sep app-advertiser demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Liftoff reaction to a Digital Turbine print; the 5 Nov peer move (+9.4%) is the nearest analogue.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed after the AppLovin/Unity rally, and DT's on-device/Android OEM business overlaps Liftoff less, so it was not a named read-through; the stock's further rise from $17.15 to $18.79 may already carry some of it.
findings.independence: Different company from finding 1; same thesis (category demand) so not additive at full weight. DT's EBITDA guide was held as margins compressed (https://finviz.com/news/419871/digital-turbine-beats-and-raises-revenue-again-but-holds-ebitda-guidance-as-margins-compress), which does not bear on Liftoff's revenue.

findings.finding: Liftoff's Q3 guide is explicitly conservative and its first public print beat by ~5.6%: Q3 revenue guided $217-222m, roughly flat on Q2's $219.5m, with the CFO calling the approach 'realistic and prudent' and saying visibility on model improvements grows as the period nears; Q2 had beaten ~$207.9m consensus by ~5.6%. A beat of the $219.5m midpoint is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue beat ~5.6% vs consensus and beat-quality was high (60% EBITDA margin), stock fell 20.59% close to close on the guide. The market did not pay for a reported-quarter beat last time.
findings.why_not_priced: A beat of the guide is largely expected (consensus $214.8-221.3m straddles the guide), so this is mostly priced; what is not priced is its size: if the market expected the Q2-style 5% beat the stock would not have needed peer prints to bounce off $14.
findings.independence: Call characterisation from https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/liftoff-mobile-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/ (prudent outlook; model gains arrived early) and Wedbush via https://finimize.com/content/wedbush-sees-liftoff-finding-growth-outside-mobile-gaming (Q3 guide = 21-24% y/y, slowdown is the World Cup comp). Same company documents as finding 4's arithmetic, different line.

findings.finding: The FY guide leaves an undemanding Q4: with H1 2026 ~ $425m (Q2 $219.5m, Q1 ~ $205m from the stated +7% q/q) and Q3 at the $219.5m midpoint, FY $870-880m implies Q4 ~ $225.5-235.5m, +5% q/q at the midpoint and ~+19% y/y on Q4 2025 ~ $194m (FY25 $686m less 9M25 $492m), while AppLovin guided Q4 +8-10% q/q and Unity guided Strategic Grow ~+20% q/q. A Q3 beat with FY held would cut the implied Q4, so the likely outcome is a FY raise at least by the beat; the guide is the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the Q3 guide implying ~1% q/q at the top end drove the -20.59% reaction despite a FY guide given at the same time; guidance is demonstrably the line.
findings.why_not_priced: The implied-Q4 arithmetic is not carried by aggregators, which list Q3 consensus only; if the street expected a FY raise of the size the peer Q4 guides imply, consensus Q3 would sit above the guide midpoint on both sources rather than $214.8m on one. The wide range reflects that Liftoff may again guide prudently (flat-ish Q4), which is what sank Q2.
findings.independence: FY25 and 9M25 revenue from https://www.mobilemarketingreads.com/?p=49905 (S-1 coverage); peer Q4 guides from https://stockanalysis.com/news/applovin-q3-2026-earnings/ and https://mobilegamer.biz/unity-posts-first-profit-since-its-ipo-as-vector-grows-126/. Shares the Q2 8-K with finding 3.

findings.finding: Non-gaming demand proxy: Q3 is football season, and sportsbooks and prediction markets ran a digital-heavy UA push (Penn's CEO forecast 'very aggressive, irrational marketing spend' this season; prediction-market digital ad spend near $200m in Jan-Jul 2026; NFL bars their TV spots so spend shifts to digital), which is the vertical Liftoff said lifted Q2 during the World Cup; offset by Wedbush's point that the World Cup makes the Q3 comparison harder.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable; Liftoff named sports betting, live scoring and prediction markets as Q2 contributors on the 12 Aug call.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission nobody has confirmed for Liftoff's share of that spend; if the market believed non-gaming kept growing after the World Cup, the 'growth outside gaming' test Wedbush named would not be framed as open.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Wedbush framing: https://finimize.com/content/wedbush-sees-liftoff-finding-growth-outside-mobile-gaming. Liftoff's own World Cup comment: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/liftoff-mobile-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/.

findings.finding: Short interest has built into the print: 3.49m shares short at the 30 Oct settlement, rising across settlements, 5.69 days to cover on a float that Blackstone (49.5%) and General Atlantic mostly lock up, with call-heavy open interest (put/call 0.40); a beat with a raise has a squeeze mechanism of its own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior squeeze on this name; Q2 reaction was -20.6% with lower short interest (DTC ~1-2 in July).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest at 5.7 days of a thin float is not in the option chain in any readable way (skew unavailable, 2,202 contracts OI, 63% spreads). Part of the short is likely a lock-up hedge that will not cover on one print, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Blackstone holding from the 13G/A https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1850351/000119312526451920/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml (2026-11-06); put/call OI from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: The stock has run about +27% from $14.79 on 30 Oct to $18.79 into the print (+9.6% in five sessions), so some of the peer-driven beat is in the price and the bar for the guide has risen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into Q2 the stock had fallen from its $28.45 high; it then dropped 20.6% on the guide. No run-up-into-print precedent yet.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself; it matters because a run-up on a peer read-through moves the reaction bar from 'any beat' to 'a raise'. Shrunk because the short interest above cuts against a negative.
findings.independence: Baseline tape run_up_5d 9.56%, run_up_20d 10.92%; StockStory 5 Nov close $17.15.

outside_window.finding: IPO lock-up expires on 30 Nov / 1 Dec 2026; Blackstone (Redbird, 83.8m shares, 49.5%) and General Atlantic can then sell down through marketed offerings that typically clear at a discount; Wedbush called it a bigger swing factor than this print. The stock is below the $23 IPO price so a price-linked early release is unlikely; terms not sourced. The overhang may cap a rally inside the window, but the supply event itself is after it.
